data.one_liner: A Dart port of FluentValidation providing chainable rule definitions for object validation.
data.what_it_does: It lets you declare validation rules for model properties using a fluent API. The validator returns a result with error details such as key, message, and code.
use_when: You need reusable, declarative validation logic separate from UI
You want chainable, readable rule definitions similar to FluentValidation in C#
You prefer a lightweight solution without code generation
avoid_when: You require built‑in UI widgets for displaying errors
You need extensive localization support (not yet implemented)
You prefer annotation‑based or code‑gen validators
strengths: Fluent, chainable API is easy to read
Supports many common validators and custom 'must' matcher
Null‑safe and works on all Flutter platforms
weaknesses: No code‑gen, so you write validators manually
Only basic validators; more complex scenarios need custom logic

alternatives.name: email_validator
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a simple email‑validation function without needing a full validation framework
